chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal, peace be upon him:
About zakat al-fitrah: Is it permissible that it be given to neighbors and close associates from among those who do not recognize and do not show enmity?
So he said: “There is no harm in that if he is in need.”

key_terms.زَكَاةِ الْفِطْرَةِ: zakat al-fitrah, the alms due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.لَا يَعْرِفُ: one who does not recognize or know, here referring to not recognizing the truth
key_terms.لَا يَنْصِبُ: one who does not show hostility or enmity

ai.seo_question: Can zakat al-fitrah be given to needy neighbors who do not recognize the Imamate but are not hostile?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning zakat al-fitrah. It indicates that giving zakat al-fitrah to neighbors or close associates who are not from among the knowing believers is permissible, so long as they are needy.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2077 - Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Imam Abu Al-Hasan Al-Awwal (as)

about Zakat al-Fitr:
"Is it permissible to give it to neighbors or close acquaintances who do not share the same beliefs or who do not acknowledge (the Imamate)?"
Imam (as) replied: "There is no harm in that if they are in need."
